title: This birdwatching expert tracked down every single bird in Grand Theft Auto VI

image.caption: A screengrab from Grand Theft Auto VI shows seagulls on the beach. Players can track down and log more than 60 birds in the new game, a side-quest that birders say is surprisingly accurate. (Rockstar Games/Grand Theft Auto VI)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

If you get tired of slinging drugs, stealing cars and running from the cops in Grand Theft Auto VI, you can always give birdwatching a try. The experience of trekking through different habitats to track down the game's dozens of species is impressively realistic, says one birdwatching expert.
If car chases are losing their thrill, players can track down dozens of birds to log instead
Getting tired of slinging drugs, stealing cars and running from the cops in Grand Theft Auto VI? You can always give birdwatching a try.

When the news dropped a week before its release that arguably the most anticipated video game of the decade would feature 62 bird species to log, birdwatching expert Nick Lund took notice — and vowed to be the first to find them all.
"I've played video games my whole life, but I'm a birder first and foremost," he told CBC's As it Happens.
"It's not often in real life that I get to rob a bank and then look at some parrots on the way out as I'm escaping."

items: Grand Theft Auto VI is the video game event of the decade

blocks.text: In the smash-hit release from Rockstar Games, players can alternate between the perspectives of characters Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as they roam a fictionalized Miami and south Florida.

As with previous games in the series, the central plotline dives into the criminal underworld. But for those who want to take their time with the crime, players can do chores, buy flowers — or go looking for avian species from roseate spoonbills to house sparrows.
Birders working to fill out their GTA VI wildlife checklists should know something I just found out: THERE’S A ZOO https://t.co/2xN0joPKcR—TheBirdist
Players can simply use in-game binoculars to look at a bird and the game automatically logs its information. Other forms of wildlife can also be logged, adding another dimension for completionists.

For Lund, the most tantalizing illegal activity the game offers isn’t smuggling or high-speed chases: it’s being able to pull his car to a screeching halt in the middle of an intersection just so he can get out and look at a cool bird in the sky.
"[It’s] something that as a real life birder I’ve wanted to do my entire life," said Lund, who lives in Maine and works for a state conservation organization.
Nick Lund, who has been birding for more than 20 years, says the birding experience in GTA VI is surprisingly accurate. (Nick Lund)
'Actual species you'd find in south Florida'
Not only do the birds in GTA VI look accurate enough for most to be identified without binoculars, Lund said, but you also have to trek to their habitats to find them.

"It's set in a fictional version of south Florida and I've birded in Florida a lot. And so I was actually able to use my experience in real Florida to figure out where to go to find birds in fake Florida GTA," he said.

blocks.text: Wading birds and herons creep through the game's version of the Everglades. Sanderlings and terns are found flitting around the beaches. Birds known to be in the north of Florida are found in the northern part of the game’s map, while bird populations that make Miami their home in real life, including tropical birds, are also found in the heart of the game’s city.
But there’s a few hiccups.
"There’s a whole bunch of whooping cranes around," Lund said. "It's a very rare bird that lives mostly in Texas."
Golden eagles are also a common sight in the game, despite being rarely spotted in south Florida.
incredibly healthy populations of critically-endangered Whooping Cranes across Vice City. Huge if true. https://t.co/doe6oMOvBX—TheBirdist
Overall, though, the game "does a great job of presenting actual species that you’d find in south Florida," Lund said.

Before the game’s release it was reported there would be 62 bird species to find — a fraction of the real number found in Florida — but the official in-game compendium only includes 60 slots for gamers to log their birds.
Lund said he’s found 63 in total so far, including three not listed in the official bird count. He’s since written a guide to the game’s birds for Audubon magazine.
He isn’t the only GTA player going gaga for gulls — many have taken to social media to share their birding excitement. One user on X suggested players "make a GTATwitter Birdwatching club!"
What makes the release of Grand Theft Auto VI so special?
"It's really wild that birding is such a prominent part of such a huge cultural phenomenon," said Kyle Horner, an engagement co-ordinator at Birds Canada.
He noted that some other games, like Rockstar’s Red Dead Redemption 2, have included birding, and said he hopes it catches on.
"Hopefully people who enjoy it in the game maybe take it up in real life. Maybe they realize there's birds outside in their own world that they can go and explore, too."
Considering the game is for entertainment and not for education, "they really nailed it," Horner added.
Players can use the in-game binoculars to automatically log birds. (Rockstar Games/Grand Theft Auto VI)
Lund doesn’t know if he was actually the first player to find all the birds, but a designer from Rockstar gave their seal of approval.
When Lund shared a video of him finding his 60th bird — an owl — senior technical designer Alec McNamara wrote "History!" in response.
